pages.title: Treehouses - Yuquiyu Farm
pages.description: Yuquiyú is a rustic retreat in the foothills of Puerto Rico’s El Yunque rainforest — a place to reawaken the senses in harmony with nature.
pages.text:
Treehouses - Yuquiyu Farm
Treehouses
Treehouses
An architecture that reflects Caribbean traditions …
We provide shelter from the sun, rain and wind in artisan-crafted treehouses with hot and cold running water, electricity, a comfortable queen-size bed, a luxurious bath, and a well-equipped kitchenette. Each treehouse is designed to accommodate only two people 18 years and older. The property also offers a pool with a wonderful view and a plunge pool to sit in and cool off.
Guests have the responsibility to be sure that Yuquiyú is appropriate to their abilities and interests. An explanation as to why Yuquiyú may  not  be suitable for some people appears on our page titled  We are not for everyone .
The treehouses at Yuquiyú are inspired by the small, wooden houses common in Puerto Rico over a century ago. Built on the side of a canyon, our humble dwellings float on pillars among the trees in one of the most scenic parts of the property — an outcropping of massive boulders. Above are the terraces for our organic garden, fruit trees and free parking; below is a cascading river and beyond is the rainforest. Click See More for more photos.
“ Less than one hour from San Juan’s airport, the Yuquiyu Treehouses are a world away from civilization and glitzy resorts … ” –Destination: Wildlife

pages.title: El Mirador Treehouse - Yuquiyu Farm
pages.text:
El Mirador Treehouse - Yuquiyu Farm
El Mirador
Named for its view of the rainforest peaks
Perched high above an outcropping of boulders with a small side garden, El Mirador (The Lookout) is named for its view of the rainforest peaks. The treehouse features 144 square feet of interior space and an 84-square-foot balcony with a commanding view of El Yunque rainforest. The private bath is on the main level and is reached by a footbridge from the balcony.  It offers a slate interior, high-end fixtures and a rain shower with an equally commanding view of the rainforest. El Mirador also gives guests a shady retreat with its own garden. See more photos below.
Each of our treehouses has one queen-size bed and is designed to accommodate only two people 18 years and older.
(When reserving a treehouse choose your arrival date and then your departure date. Ex.: A two night stay would require 3 gold days.)

La Cara de Indio Treehouse - Yuquiyu Farm
La Cara de Indio
Named after a Taino petroglyph
Surrounded by palms, mango trees and lush tropical plants, La Cara de Indio (The Indian Face) is named after a Taino petroglyph not far from the property. The treehouse features 144 square feet of interior space and an 84-square-foot balcony overlooking a panorama of El Yunque rainforest. Below the main level of the treehouse and reached by a short gravel path is a 90-square-foot, private bath that offers a slate interior, high-end fixtures and a rain shower with a similar view of the rainforest. See more photos below.
Each of our treehouses has one queen-size bed and is designed to accommodate only two people 18 years and older.
(When reserving a treehouse choose your arrival date and then your departure date. Ex.: A two night stay would require 3 gold days.)

La Cascada Treehouse - Yuquiyu Farm
La Cascada
Named for the cascading river below
Within a grove of Royal Palms and vanilla orchids, La Cascada (The Cascade) is named for the cascading river below. The treehouse features 121 square feet of interior space and a 176-square-foot balcony. The view of El Yunque rainforest and the river is majestic. Below the main level and reached by a stairway from the balcony is a 81-square-foot, private bath that offers a slate interior, high-end fixtures and a rain shower with an equally spectacular view. See more photos below.
Each of our treehouses has one queen-size bed and is designed to accommodate only two people 18 years and older.
